title: SEC1: bt5.4 node_id.bin deletion = silent identity change
description: bt5.4 persists node_id to node_id.bin in the data directory. If deleted or replaced (backup restore, disk corruption, container re-image), the daemon auto-generates a new random ID on next start with only an info-level log line ('generated and saved new node_id'). There is no error-level log, no metrics counter, and no startup health check that compares the new ID against any stored reference. The HLC node_id is a tiebreaker in timestamp ordering; a silently changed ID does not break correctness but will cause HLC timestamps from the same wall+logical tick to produce a different ordering for a given peer, potentially causing group-log reconcile divergence that is hard to diagnose. Mitigation: (a) emit a warn-level log if no prior ID file existed on a production-looking config (signing_key_path set), or (b) add a node_id_expected field to config so operators can pin the value without relying solely on the file, or (c) document explicitly in the operator guide that node_id.bin loss requires manual log reconcile.
